findings.reason: The stored description itself says 'Mobility and stability exercise for the shoulders'. A plate halo is a shoulder mobility/stability drill, not metabolic conditioning.
Rectus abdominis is stored as the PRIMARY mover of a plate halo. The plate is circled around the head by the shoulder girdle; the trunk is braced isometrically and is not the prime mover.
Rectus abdominis is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a step-up alongside gluteus maximus and vastus lateralis, with placeholder low/low/low tension. It produces none of the recorded hip/knee extension.
In an arch (superman) hold the trunk is actively EXTENDED; rectus abdominis is the antagonist, yet it is stored as a primary mover with placeholder low/low/low tension.

An archer push-up shifts most of the bodyweight onto one arm and is a recognised advanced push-up progression; it cannot share the 'low' technical demand assigned to the knee push-up in the same sample.

findings.proposed: deltoid_lateral -> primary; trapezius_middle -> stabilizer; latissimus_dorsi -> remove
findings.reason: Middle trapezius is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a front/lateral raise (it is a scapular retractor, not a humeral elevator), the lateral deltoid - the actual prime mover of abduction - is only secondary, and latissimus dorsi, a shoulder adductor and direct antagonist, is stored as a contributor.
Anterior deltoid is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a sit-up, on a par with rectus abdominis. The only recorded joint action is spine_flexion, which the deltoid cannot produce.

Anterior deltoid is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a shrug. Scapular elevation is produced by the upper trapezius and levator scapulae; the anterior deltoid acts at the glenohumeral joint and plays no role.
Rectus abdominis is stored as a primary mover of a backward sled march driven by hip and knee extension, while the quadriceps - the prime mover of backward dragging - is only secondary.

Rectus abdominis is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a barbell deadlift, level with gluteus maximus and biceps femoris. The stored joint action for the trunk is spine_anti_flexion, i.e. an explicitly isometric bracing role.

Biceps brachii long head is stored as a PRIMARY mover and brachialis as a secondary mover of a wrist curl. Both are elbow flexors, neither crosses the wrist, and the forearms rest on the thighs so the elbow does not move.
The stored description states the exercise is 'performed unilaterally to emphasize dorsal contraction', yet unilateral=false and side_mode=none, so it can never be logged per side.
Erector spinae is stored as a secondary mover with high midrange and shortened tension in a movement whose only joint action is spine_flexion; the spinal extensors are the antagonist here.
Rectus abdominis is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a dumbbell overhead press, level with the anterior deltoid, while the triceps - which produce the recorded elbow extension - are only secondary.

A power clean is driven by explosive hip and knee triple extension, yet gluteus maximus and vastus lateralis are stored only as secondary while rectus abdominis is a primary mover with placeholder moderate/moderate/moderate tension.

A pullover is shoulder extension/adduction with the elbow angle held fixed. Latissimus dorsi is the prime mover but is stored as secondary, while the triceps long head is stored as primary; the stored joint actions (elbow_extension, shoulder_horizontal_adduction) describe a press, not a pullover.
Tibialis anterior is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a calf raise. It is the dorsiflexor and therefore the direct antagonist of the recorded ankle_plantar_flexion.
Anterior deltoid is stored as a PRIMARY mover of an overhead triceps extension whose only joint action is elbow_extension; the shoulder is held still, so the deltoid contributes no motion.

The entire muscle set for a clean & jerk is the pressing chain (deltoid, triceps, pectoralis); no hip or knee extensor is linked at all, although both the clean and the dip-drive of the jerk are produced by lower-body triple extension.
High knees is running in place with no external load; resistance_source is already bodyweight_leverage, so bodyweight=false contradicts the rest of the row.

Rectus abdominis is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a barbell hip thrust with high tension in the shortened position; there the abdominal wall braces against lumbar hyperextension, it does not produce the hip extension.
Latissimus dorsi is stored as a contributing muscle of an overhead press. The lat extends and adducts the shoulder and is the antagonist of the recorded shoulder_flexion.

The exercise is a selectorised lever crunch machine with a chest pad; resistance comes from the weight stack, not from body leverage. The tracking profile is wrong for the same reason (bodyweight_reps / none / bodyweight_aware instead of weight_reps / total_load / equipment_instance).
A neck harness is loaded with hanging plates; there is no cam machine involved, and the equipment row (back_extension_machine) is unrelated to the exercise.
Splenius capitis and splenius cervicis are stored as PRIMARY movers of neck FLEXION. Both are cervical extensors and are the direct antagonists of the stored joint action.

tracking_type=weight_reps with total_load implies a numeric weight is logged, but the resistance is a band; comparison_scope is already non_comparable and other band exercises in the sample store reps / none.

The only muscle linked to a side plank is rectus abdominis. A side plank resists lateral flexion in the frontal plane; the prime stabilisers are the obliques and quadratus lumborum, none of which are present.
weight_reps + total_load on a loop-band abduction implies a loggable weight that does not exist; comparison_scope is already non_comparable.
Gluteus maximus is stored as a PRIMARY mover of an exercise whose only joint action is knee_flexion; the glute does not cross the knee. The medial hamstrings, actual knee flexors, are absent.
Latissimus dorsi is stored as a contributing muscle of a standing overhead press; it is a shoulder extensor/adductor and therefore the antagonist of the recorded shoulder_flexion.

An ab-wheel rollout carries no external load; resistance_source is already bodyweight_leverage and the tracking profile is bodyweight_reps / none / bodyweight_aware, so bodyweight=false contradicts the row.

Erector spinae is stored as a PRIMARY mover of an anti-extension rollout, level with rectus abdominis. The rollout is precisely the exercise in which the abdominal wall resists the pull of the spinal extensors.

The only muscles linked to battle rope waves are rectus abdominis and the obliques; the alternating waves are produced by repeated shoulder flexion/extension and no shoulder or arm musculature is present at all.
resistance_source=bodyweight_leverage and the tracking profile is bodyweight_reps / none / bodyweight_aware, but bodyweight=false; a tuck front lever row uses no external load.
Latissimus dorsi is completely absent from a front lever row - the single most important muscle of the movement - while teres major is the only primary listed.

Same defect as barbell_wrist_curl_v_2: biceps brachii long head is a PRIMARY mover and brachialis a secondary mover of a wrist curl, although neither crosses the wrist and the only joint action is wrist_flexion.

non_vocabulary_findings.problem: Joint action is spine_anti_extension and the pattern is anti_extension, but an arch body hold is active spinal EXTENSION (spine_extension / spinal_extension exist in the vocabulary). Equipment is also wrong: dip_bars + pull_up_bar are linked to a floor-based prone hold.
The stored joint action is neck_flexion although the exercise is lateral neck flexion; the vocabulary contains neck_lateral_flexion, so the stored action contradicts the movement.

The description says the movement pushes a weighted sled, but the only equipment linked is a resistance band (the sled is missing), and tracking_type=weight_distance is combined with load_input_mode=none, so no load can ever be recorded.

The only equipment linked is pull_up_bar although the description says the exercise is a hang clean and overhead press of a BARBELL. The stored joint actions likewise cover only the jerk (shoulder flexion / elbow extension) and omit the hip hinge that the movement pattern records.
No equipment is linked although the description says the exercise is performed 'while hanging from a pull-up bar'; a bar is mandatory to perform it at all.
The only equipment linked is box_plyo for an exercise described as 'running in place', and all 11 linked muscles carry placeholder low/low/low tension in all three ranges.

The movement pattern is vertical_press and the joint actions are elbow_extension / shoulder_flexion / scapula_elevation, but a windmill holds the bell statically overhead while the trunk laterally flexes and the hips hinge; no press occurs. spine_lateral_flexion and hip_hinge exist in the vocabulary and are unused.
The linked equipment is back_extension_machine for a machine that trains trunk FLEXION.

The movement pattern is rotation and the only joint action is spine_rotation, but the exercise is a two-handed medicine-ball CHEST PUSH; the stored primary muscles (pectoralis major, triceps) confirm a horizontal press, which the recorded actions contradict.
The movement pattern is rotation and the only joint action is spine_rotation; an overhead slam is shoulder extension plus spinal FLEXION in the sagittal plane, with no rotation component.

The movement pattern is horizontal_press and the joint actions are shoulder_horizontal_adduction / scapula_protraction, but the description is an overhead VERTICAL press; vertical_press and shoulder_flexion exist in the vocabulary and are used by every other overhead press in the sample.

The description ('lying on your back with legs extended, flexing the knees') describes a supine curl rather than the kneeling nordic-style inverse leg curl the name denotes, and the linked equipment is leg_curl_machine_lying although the exercise is self-assisted and needs no machine.

The movement pattern is locomotion:primary for a 45-degree leg press machine; the pattern should be squat (used by every other leg press in the sample), and the linked equipment is the generic 'sled' rather than a leg press machine.
The equipment is cable_attachment_rope (a cable-machine rope handle) rather than a battle rope, and the only joint action is spine_rotation although the waves are sagittal-plane shoulder movements.

The row has no movement pattern, no joint action and a NULL kinetic_chain, so the movement is structurally undescribed; every other exercise in the sample carries at least one pattern and one joint action.
